title: Hamiltonicity of regular sublinear expanders
summary: We say that a $d$-regular graph is a $γ$-expander if for every not too large set of vertices $S$, there are at least $γd |S|$ edges leaving $S$, and we say that a graph $G$ is $γ$-far from bipartite if at least $γe(G)$ edges need to be removed to make it bipartite. We prove that there exists an absolute constant $K$ such that any $n$-vertex $d$-regular $γ$-expander with $d \ge (γ^{-1} \log n)^K$ is Hamiltonian, provided that it is bipartite or $γ$-far from bipartite.
